title: Instances where Rule Had Been Waived for 80% of Funds Raised for Foreign Charitable Purposes to be Applied towards Local Charitable Purposes
what_it_is: Instances where Rule Had Been Waived for 80% of Funds Raised for Foreign Charitable Purposes to be Applied towards Local Charitable Purposes

sections.label: Charities fund-raising rule waivers
sections.summary: The Commissioner of Charities granted about 70 waivers of the 80:20 fund-raising rule yearly, mostly for private appeals and disaster relief.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
sentences.text: In the past five years, the Commissioner of Charities (COC) has, on average, granted about 70 waivers of the 80:20 fund-raising rule each year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
sentences.text: More than 70% of the waivers were granted for private appeals such as within schools, churches and other organisations to support charitable work in other countries such as school programmes or missionary work.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
sentences.text: The majority of the remaining appeals granted waivers were for disaster and humanitarian relief efforts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
sentences.text: For example, in 2022, there were 56 waivers granted for private appeals, while 16 permits granted with waivers were for humanitarian relief, such as for the crisis in Ukraine, and natural disasters such as the Pakistan floods and earthquakes in Afghanistan and Indonesia.

sections.label: Overseas fund-raising permit criteria
sections.summary: Seven permits were issued for Türkiye and Syria earthquake fund-raising, with waivers, and permit holders must meet AMLCFT, harmony and foreign law criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: We do this in order to mitigate risks and also to reduce restrictions faced during the fund-raising process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: I wanted to give the Member an update that, for example, the COC has already issued seven permits thus far for fund-raising efforts for the earthquakes in Türkiye and Syria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The organisations are: the Singapore Red Cross Society, Rahmatan Lil Alamin Foundation Limited, Mercy Relief Limited, Operation Mobilisation Singapore Limited, World Vision International, Bible Society of Singapore, Buddhist Tzu Chi Merit Organization (Singapore) Limited.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: In fact, COC granted waiver of the 80:20 rule for all of these permits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Talking about the criteria, well, given that the funds raised will be used to support overseas beneficiaries, permit holders must: first, have in place an anti-money laundering and countering of the financing of terrorism (AMLCFT) policy; two, exercise sensitivity when conducting its fund-raising activities and also not engage in any activities that may undermine the social and racial religious harmony in Singapore; and three, ensure that the funds raised are used by its beneficiaries in conformity with the laws of their respective countries and in a manner that would not affect Singapore's bilateral relations with these countries.
